_about: UK decision trees. MHRA applies the EU variations classification guidelines of 2013 (2013/C 223/01) to UK marketing authorisations until it issues its own; these trees follow them. allOf nodes list the guideline conditions in paraphrase: read the official text for exact wording. Changes not listed here are not modelled in this edition.

fail.why: A condition is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of the Variations Regulation as it applies in the UK).

yes.note: Simplified: the 2013 guidelines have no separate entry for biological reference standards.

For chemical products a new lot of an in-house standard qualified under GMP needs no variation.
no.note: Simplified: if the dossier itself changes, classify that change instead.

tree.why: An editorial change to the product information on its own is not listed. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of the Variations Regulation as it applies in the UK).

fail.why: A condition is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of the Variations Regulation as it applies in the UK).

agreed.why: Implementing RMP wording already agreed by MHRA is Type IA-IN.

minor.why: An RMP change needing minor assessment has no entry of its own in the 2013 guidelines. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of the Variations Regulation as it applies in the UK).

new.why: An RMP change that needs new data is Type II.

yes.why: Implementing the outcome needs new data: Type II.
Implementing the agreed outcome with exactly the agreed wording is Type IA-IN.

no.why: Agreed wording that needs some assessment is not listed separately in the 2013 guidelines. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of the Variations Regulation as it applies in the UK).

tree.why: Deleting an indication is Type IB.

The 2013 guidelines have no product lifecycle management document or established conditions, and MHRA has not issued its own procedure. Ask MHRA (for example through scientific advice) how to agree them; until then, changes are classified with the usual entries.
tree.note: The EU introduced the PLCM document in its 2025 guidelines (Q.II.g.6); this is one of the clearest UK and EU differences.

tree.why: Without a PLCM document in the 2013 guidelines there is nothing to update; classify the underlying change with the usual entries.

The 2013 guidelines do not use established conditions: any change to what the dossier describes is a variation, classified with the usual entries. Changes to things the dossier does not describe need none.

delete.why: Deleting an approved PACMP is Type IA-IN.

minor.why: A minor change that does not alter the strategy of the PACMP is Type IB.

major.why: A major change to an approved PACMP is Type II.

yes.why: Introducing a material of human or animal origin that needs a viral safety or TSE assessment is Type II.
A raw material change that may significantly affect the quality of a biological active substance is Type II.

no.why: A raw material change with no significant impact is not listed. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of the Variations Regulation as it applies in the UK).

lifetime.why: A minor change to the purification of a biological active substance is not listed as Type IA in the 2013 guidelines. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of the Variations Regulation as it applies in the UK).

supplier.why: A different resin or supplier changes a purification step of a biological active substance: Type II.

first.why: Studies on steps tested for the first time are Type II.

higher.why: Replacing studies with a modified risk assessment is Type II.

same.why: Replacing obsolete studies without a modified risk assessment is Type IB.

tree.why: A new UK contact on the leaflet or label, with the SmPC unchanged, goes to MHRA as a labelling notification rather than a variation (the UK counterpart of Article 61(3)).
tree.note: A new QPPV or UK pharmacovigilance contact is updated in the pharmacovigilance system master file and with MHRA, with no variation.

strength.why: Deleting a strength is Type IB.

pass.why: Deleting a pack size, with the remaining sizes fitting the dosing, is Type IA.

fail.why: A condition is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of the Variations Regulation as it applies in the UK).
